title: GPX Timestamp Span Calculator: First to Last
description: Calculate the time span between the earliest and latest timestamps in a GPX file with the GPX Timestamp Span Calculator. Free, local.
summary_sentence: For example, stamps running from 2026-10-04T07:00:00Z to 11:24:36Z span 15,876 seconds — 4 hours, 24 minutes, 36 seconds — the recording's full window on the clock.
quick_answer: The GPX Timestamp Span Calculator computes the elapsed time between the earliest and latest timestamps anywhere in a GPX file. Load the file locally and read the span with its endpoints — the window durations and averages are built from.

popular_table.note: GPX timestamps are UTC ISO 8601 instants. Local readings of the endpoints depend on the viewer's zone; the span between them never does.

faq: What if only some points carry timestamps?
The span is computed from the stamps that exist. Points without <time> neither extend nor shrink the window — and their existence is worth knowing, since time-based tools will skip them silently.
A single timestamp in the whole file?
The span is zero — one instant makes a window of no width. The tool reports the instant and the zero honestly.
The span covers the whole gulf, days included. Whether that is one expedition or two files' accident is context the reader supplies.
Honoured where present — some devices stamp tenths. The span's precision follows the file's finest stamps.
Sloppy writers omit the Z or write offsets. The span arithmetic treats the stamps as one consistent frame; if a file mixes frames, its window is unreliable in a way no calculator can launder.
No — earliest-to-latest is positive by construction. A file whose document order runs backwards still yields its true positive window, with the disorder visible in its endpoints.
